notes: 40 Easy + 10 Normal. Easy is 16 landmark / 24 urban, which holds the easy tier's landmark share near 48% against a 35% floor and keeps landmark+urban at 100% against an 80% floor, with no remote entries at all. The 24 urban Easy candidates are distinctive city centres rather than world landmarks, so the batch is geographically diverse instead of being a list of famous monuments. The 10 Normal are 4 rural / 3 suburban / 3 urban, continuing to protect the Normal rural+remote floor. No panoId appears here: one may only come from a real verification run.

candidates.label: Plaza de Armas, Arequipa
candidates.source: Plaza de Armas, Arequipa, arcaded in white sillar volcanic stone.
candidates.rationale: Easy: a white volcanic-stone colonnade under a snow-capped volcano is unmistakable once seen. 1000 km from the Cusco entry.

candidates.label: Plaza 25 de Mayo, Sucre
candidates.source: Plaza 25 de Mayo, the central square of Sucre.
candidates.rationale: Easy: uniformly whitewashed colonial arcades around a formal plaza — visually striking and easy to reason to Andean South America.

candidates.label: Avenida San Martín, Ushuaia
candidates.source: Avenida San Martín, the main street of Ushuaia, Tierra del Fuego.
candidates.rationale: Easy: a Spanish-signed town beneath snow peaks at the end of the continent — the combination of latitude cues and language makes it solvable quickly.

candidates.label: Teatro Amazonas, Manaus
candidates.source: The square in front of the Teatro Amazonas opera house, Manaus.
candidates.rationale: Easy: a pink Belle Époque opera house in the middle of the Amazon. 2700 km from any other Brazilian entry.

candidates.label: Plaza Muñoz Gamero, Punta Arenas
candidates.source: Plaza Muñoz Gamero, central Punta Arenas, Magallanes.
candidates.rationale: Easy: grand Patagonian mansions around a cypress-planted square — distinctive and clearly far south. 2000 km from Valparaíso.

candidates.label: Calle del Recuerdo, Guatapé
candidates.source: Calle del Recuerdo, Guatapé, Antioquia, with its painted zócalo panels.
candidates.rationale: Easy: every building base is covered in coloured relief panels — one of the most visually distinctive streetscapes anywhere, and not a monument.

candidates.label: Plaza Bolívar, Mérida
candidates.source: Plaza Bolívar, central Mérida, Venezuelan Andes.
candidates.rationale: Easy: a colonial plaza under high Andean peaks. Venezuela's first catalog entry, which is why it belongs in the easy tier rather than the hard one.

candidates.label: Stabroek Market, Georgetown
candidates.source: Water Street at Stabroek Market, Georgetown.
candidates.rationale: Easy: a cast-iron colonial market hall with a clock tower, English signage, tropical light. Distinctive, and Guyana is a new country for the catalog.

candidates.label: Jardín de la Unión, Guanajuato
candidates.source: Jardín de la Unión, the central plaza of Guanajuato.
candidates.rationale: Easy: laurel-shaded plaza against a baroque theatre and coloured hillside houses. 350 km from Querétaro.

candidates.label: Plaza Mayor, Trinidad
candidates.source: Plaza Mayor, Trinidad, Sancti Spíritus.
candidates.rationale: Easy if it exists at all: pastel colonial facades and cobbles. Cuba lost its only entry when the Malecón failed, and official coverage there is doubtful — this is a deliberate second and final test of the country.

candidates.label: Bull Street, Savannah
candidates.source: Bull Street through the historic squares of Savannah, Georgia.
candidates.rationale: Easy: live oaks hung with Spanish moss over antebellum townhouses — a look that exists in one part of one country.

candidates.label: Government Street, Victoria
candidates.source: Government Street through downtown Victoria, British Columbia.
candidates.rationale: Easy: hanging flower baskets, Edwardian stone and a harbour full of floatplanes — visibly Canadian-Pacific. Replaces a Petit-Champlain candidate the collision check found 120 m from the Château Frontenac entry.

candidates.label: Calle Centro América, Flores
candidates.source: Calle Centro América on the island town of Flores, Petén.
candidates.rationale: Easy: brightly painted low houses on a lake island, all visibly surrounded by water. Distinctive without being a monument.

candidates.label: Burns Avenue, San Ignacio
candidates.source: Burns Avenue, San Ignacio, Cayo District.
candidates.rationale: Easy: English signage in a Central American tropical town is a giveaway combination found essentially only in Belize. New country for the catalog.

candidates.label: Handelskade, Willemstad
candidates.source: Handelskade waterfront, Punda, Willemstad.
candidates.rationale: Easy: Dutch gabled facades painted in pastel on a Caribbean harbour. Unambiguous, and a new country for the catalog.

candidates.label: Cais da Ribeira, Porto
candidates.source: Cais da Ribeira on the Douro waterfront, Porto.
candidates.rationale: Easy: tiled riverfront houses under the Dom Luís bridge. 300 km from Lisbon.

candidates.label: Quai de la Poissonnerie, Colmar
candidates.source: Quai de la Poissonnerie, the Petite Venise quarter of Colmar, Alsace.
candidates.rationale: Easy: half-timbered coloured houses over a canal, with French signage — the German-looking architecture plus French text is a strong, solvable combination.

candidates.label: Seestraße, Hallstatt
candidates.source: Seestraße along the lakefront at Hallstatt, Upper Austria.
candidates.rationale: Easy: timber houses stacked between a lake and a cliff. 250 km from the Schönbrunn entry.

candidates.label: Kramgasse, Bern
candidates.source: Kramgasse, the arcaded main street of Bern's old town.
candidates.rationale: Easy: 6 km of sandstone arcades with painted fountains down the middle. 100 km from the Zurich entry.

candidates.label: Binnenpad, Giethoorn
candidates.source: Binnenpad, the canal path through Giethoorn, Overijssel.
candidates.rationale: Easy: thatched cottages, footbridges and no roads. Distinctly Dutch and 120 km from Amsterdam.

candidates.label: Markt, Bruges
candidates.source: The Markt square below the belfry, Bruges.
candidates.rationale: Easy: stepped gables around a square under a leaning belfry. Belgium's first catalog entry.

candidates.label: Royal Crescent, Bath
candidates.source: Royal Crescent, Bath, Somerset.
candidates.rationale: Easy: a 150 m sweep of identical Georgian stone terraces. 170 km from London.

candidates.label: Quay Street, Galway
candidates.source: Quay Street, the Latin Quarter of Galway.
candidates.rationale: Easy: brightly painted pub frontage with bilingual Irish and English signage — the bilingual signs settle the country outright. Ireland missed once on a Connemara road 60 km west.

candidates.label: Bryggen, Bergen
candidates.source: The Bryggen wharf frontage, Bergen.
candidates.rationale: Easy: a row of leaning wooden gabled warehouses on a harbour. 300 km from Flåm.

candidates.label: Stora Torget, Visby
candidates.source: Stora Torget in the walled town of Visby, Gotland.
candidates.rationale: Easy: a medieval walled Baltic town with ruined stone churches. 200 km from Stockholm, and Sweden's second attempt after a highland road failed.

candidates.label: Jokikatu, Porvoo
candidates.source: Jokikatu along the old town riverside, Porvoo.
candidates.rationale: Easy: ochre timber warehouses on a river bank with Finnish and Swedish signage. 50 km from Helsinki — outside the cluster radius.

candidates.label: Līvu laukums, Riga
candidates.source: Līvu laukums in Riga's old town.
candidates.rationale: Easy: art-nouveau and Hanseatic facades around a broad square. Latvia's first catalog entry.

candidates.label: Pilies gatvė, Vilnius
candidates.source: Pilies gatvė, the main old-town street of Vilnius.
candidates.rationale: Easy: baroque church facades along a curving cobbled street. Lithuania's first catalog entry.

candidates.label: Cankarjevo nabrežje, Ljubljana
candidates.source: Cankarjevo nabrežje along the Ljubljanica river.
candidates.rationale: Easy: pastel riverfront terraces under a castle hill, with distinctive Plečnik bridges. Slovenia's first catalog entry.

candidates.label: Grisia street, Rovinj
candidates.source: Grisia, the stepped street climbing the Rovinj peninsula, Istria.
candidates.rationale: Easy: Venetian-Istrian stone lanes rising to a campanile. 700 km from the Dubrovnik entry.

candidates.label: Avenue Oqba Ibn Nafiaa, Essaouira
candidates.source: Avenue Oqba Ibn Nafiaa along the Essaouira ramparts.
candidates.rationale: Easy: blue-and-white medina walls on an Atlantic seafront. Distinctive, and 400 km from the Midelt hard candidate.

candidates.label: Kenyatta Road, Stone Town
candidates.source: Kenyatta Road, Stone Town, Zanzibar.
candidates.rationale: Easy: coral-stone Swahili architecture with carved doors. Tanzania missed once on a Kilimanjaro road 500 km away; Stone Town is a dense named urban area.

candidates.label: Rue Blaise Diagne, Saint-Louis
candidates.source: Rue Blaise Diagne on the island of Saint-Louis, Senegal.
candidates.rationale: Easy: colonial balconied townhouses in faded ochre with French signage in West Africa — a specific, readable combination. 250 km from Dakar.

candidates.label: Lalibela town road, Amhara
candidates.source: The main town road through Lalibela, Amhara region.
candidates.rationale: Easy in the sense the tier requires — Amharic script is unique to Ethiopia and Eritrea, so the view is quickly solvable. Ethiopia's first catalog entry.

candidates.label: Durbar Square, Bhaktapur
candidates.source: The vehicle-accessible edge of Bhaktapur Durbar Square, Kathmandu valley.
candidates.rationale: Easy: tiered pagoda temples and carved brick — visually unique to the Kathmandu valley. Replaces a Lijiang candidate: mainland China has no Google Street View car coverage, so it was a near-certain ZERO_RESULTS. The coordinate is on the square edge rather than inside it, because pedestrian precincts are what defeated the repair batch.

candidates.label: Lyab-i Hauz, Bukhara
candidates.source: The Lyab-i Hauz pool and madrasas, Bukhara.
candidates.rationale: Easy: tiled madrasa portals around a stone pool. Uzbekistan's first catalog entry, and visually unlike anywhere else in Asia.

candidates.label: Fort Road, Jaisalmer
candidates.source: Fort Road below the Jaisalmer fort walls, Rajasthan.
candidates.rationale: Easy: a golden sandstone fort rising straight out of the desert. India's second entry alongside the Leh hard candidate, 900 km apart.

candidates.label: Church Street, Galle Fort
candidates.source: Church Street inside Galle Fort, southern Sri Lanka.
candidates.rationale: Easy: Dutch colonial verandahs and rampart walls in the tropics. 120 km from Colombo.

candidates.label: High Street, Fremantle
candidates.source: High Street, Fremantle, Western Australia.
candidates.rationale: Easy: an intact Victorian port streetscape with wide verandahs and left-hand traffic. 2000 km from any other Australian entry.

candidates.label: Beach Street, Levuka
candidates.source: Beach Street, Levuka, Ovalau island.
candidates.rationale: Easy: a colonial timber shopfront row facing a Pacific beach. Fiji has missed twice on road coordinates; a named heritage street is the method's proper test.

candidates.label: Dobó tér, Eger
candidates.source: Dobó tér, the central square of Eger.
candidates.rationale: Normal, not easy: baroque facades and a Hungarian-signed square that could be Slovakia or Austria at a glance. The Budapest Chain Bridge is the easy Hungarian view.

candidates.label: Rynek Wielki, Zamość
candidates.source: Rynek Wielki, the arcaded renaissance market square of Zamość.
candidates.rationale: Normal: an Italianate square in eastern Poland — the architecture argues for Italy and the signage against it. 240 km from Lublin.

candidates.label: Rua de Santa Maria, Guimarães
candidates.source: Rua de Santa Maria, the medieval street of Guimarães, Minho.
candidates.rationale: Normal: granite and whitewash in a narrow northern Portuguese lane. Portuguese signage settles the country; the town does not announce itself. 50 km from Porto.

candidates.label: Calle Topete, Todos Santos
candidates.source: Calle Topete, Todos Santos, Baja California Sur.
candidates.rationale: Normal: a low desert town of painted adobe and palms. Mexican but placeable only to 'somewhere on the Pacific side'. 1000 km from Guerrero Negro.

candidates.label: Highland Avenue, Marfa
candidates.source: Highland Avenue, Marfa, west Texas.
candidates.rationale: Normal: a high-desert town with a domed courthouse and wide empty streets. 80 km from the Van Horn hard candidate, so a separate cluster.

candidates.label: Church Street, Prince Albert
candidates.source: Church Street, Prince Albert, at the foot of the Swartberg, Western Cape.
candidates.rationale: Normal: Karoo cottages with white gables under bare mountains. More built form and more signage than the hard Karoo entries, less than a town centre.

candidates.label: Kenyatta Avenue, Nanyuki
candidates.source: Kenyatta Avenue, Nanyuki, Laikipia, on the equator below Mount Kenya.
candidates.rationale: Normal: an upcountry Kenyan town street with English and Swahili signage. Kenya has now missed three times on approximate coordinates — this is the first named-street attempt, and if it fails the country should be set aside.

candidates.label: Bạch Đằng, Da Nang
candidates.source: Bạch Đằng riverside street, central Da Nang.
candidates.rationale: Normal: a modern Vietnamese riverfront with heavy scooter traffic. The diacritics settle the country; the city is one of several. 30 km from Hội An — outside the cluster radius.

candidates.label: Jalan Ahmad Yani, Bukittinggi
candidates.source: Jalan Ahmad Yani, central Bukittinggi, West Sumatra.
candidates.rationale: Normal: a highland Sumatran town with Minangkabau roof forms among ordinary shophouses. Indonesian signage narrows the country, the island is the real question.

candidates.label: Rizal Boulevard, Dumaguete
candidates.source: Rizal Boulevard, the seafront promenade of Dumaguete, Negros Oriental.
candidates.rationale: Normal: acacia-shaded seafront with English signage. 100 km from Bacolod and visually unremarkable — the tier turns on recognising the Philippines, not the town.
